tool.name: OptimizeCompression
tool.summary: Creates optimized, compressed Cloud Optimized GeoTIFFs (COGs) with intelligent defaults and expert-level automation.

usage.bullet_item: Product Type determines intelligent defaults for compression, raster type, and processing parameters.
For elevation products (DEM type), Vertical SRS is required to create proper compound coordinate systems.
The tool automatically selects optimal compression settings based on product type, but you can override any parameter.
JPEG and JXL are recommended for multi-band imagery; DEFLATE, ZSTD, or LERC for elevation/scientific data.
The tool generates a comparison report showing before/after analysis and validates the output as a proper COG.
All processing is performed in-memory using GDAL's virtual file system for maximum performance.

param.name: input_path
param.displayname: Input GeoTIFF, Raster Layer, or Folder
param.dialogReference: Source GeoTIFF file to optimize and compress. Can be any valid GeoTIFF including DEMs, imagery, or thematic data.

param.name: output_path
param.dialogReference: Path for the optimized output file. The tool will create a Cloud Optimized GeoTIFF (COG) with compression and proper internal structure.

param.name: product_type
param.dialogReference: Type of GeoTIFF product. This determines intelligent defaults for compression algorithm, raster type (PixelIsPoint vs PixelIsArea), and processing parameters. Choose 'dem' for elevation models, 'image' for imagery/orthophotos, 'error' for uncertainty/error models, 'scientific' for general scientific data, or 'thematic' for classified/categorical data.

param.name: vertical_srs
param.dialogReference: Vertical spatial reference system for elevation products. REQUIRED for DEM product type. Can be an EPSG code (e.g., 'EPSG:5703'), vertical datum name (e.g., 'NAVD88', 'EGM2008'), or WKT string. This creates proper compound coordinate systems and prevents vertical datum errors.

param.name: algorithm
param.dialogReference: Compression algorithm to use. Leave blank for automatic selection based on product type. JPEG (lossy) and JXL (lossy/lossless) are best for imagery. DEFLATE, ZSTD, and LZW are lossless algorithms suitable for DEMs. LERC supports controlled lossy compression for floating-point data. NONE creates uncompressed output.

param.name: raster_type
param.dialogReference: Override the raster type assignment. Choose 'point' for PixelIsPoint (pixel represents a point sample) or 'area' for PixelIsArea (pixel represents an averaged area). Leave blank to use intelligent defaults: DEMs default to 'area', imagery to 'point'.

param.name: nodata
param.dialogReference: NoData value to assign to the output. Use this to remap problematic NoData values (e.g., -9999, -3.4e38) to standard values like NaN for floating-point data or appropriate values for integer data. Leave blank to preserve the input NoData value.

param.name: decimals
param.dialogReference: Number of decimal places to round floating-point data. Rounding significantly improves compression efficiency by removing pseudo-precision. Recommended: 2 decimals (1 cm precision) for DEMs, 1 decimal (10 cm) for error models. Leave blank for no rounding.

param.name: quality
param.dialogReference: Quality setting for JPEG or JXL compression (75-100). Default is 90, which provides visually lossless results for most imagery. Higher values (95-99) reduce artifacts but increase file size. Lower values (75-85) increase compression but may show visible artifacts.

param.name: predictor
param.dialogReference: Predictor for LZW/DEFLATE/ZSTD compression. Leave blank for automatic selection. Predictor 2 (horizontal differencing) is best for integer and rounded floating-point data. Predictor 3 (floating-point) is best for unrounded floating-point data. Predictor 1 (none) disables prediction.

param.name: max_z_error
param.dialogReference: Maximum allowed error for LERC compression in the same units as the data. Use 0 for lossless LERC. For elevation in meters, 0.01 = 1 cm precision. WARNING: Do not use lossy LERC on hydro-conditioned DEMs as it may alter flow directions.

param.name: level
param.dialogReference: Compression level for DEFLATE (1-9) or ZSTD (1-22). Higher values provide better compression but slower encoding. Leave blank for automatic selection: DEFLATE=6, ZSTD=9.

param.name: tile_size
param.dialogReference: Tile size in pixels for the primary image and overviews. Default is 512. Use 256 for web mapping, 512 for general use, or 1024 for large images or processing workflows.

param.name: mask_nodata
param.dialogReference: Add NoData pixels to the transparency mask. Leave blank for automatic behavior based on product type (enabled for imagery, disabled for DEMs).

param.name: mask_alpha
param.displayname: Convert Alpha Band (if one exists) to Internal Mask
param.dialogReference: Convert RGBA imagery to RGB with internal transparency mask. A 1-bit transparency mask is more efficient than an 8-bit alpha band and fixes edge effects with JPEG compression. Recommended for imagery. Does not apply if input has no alpha band.

param.name: cog
param.dialogReference: Create a Cloud Optimized GeoTIFF with proper internal structure for efficient HTTP range requests and web streaming. Recommended for all outputs.

param.name: overviews
param.dialogReference: Generate internal overview pyramids (reduced-resolution versions) for efficient visualization at multiple scales. Highly recommended for web mapping and large files.

param.name: geo_metadata
param.displayname: Write External XML to GEO_METADATA Tag
param.dialogReference: Write external XML sidecar files (.xml) to the internal GEO_METADATA TIFF tag (#50909). This embeds metadata directly in the file for better portability.

param.name: write_pam_xml
param.dialogReference: Write an Esri-compatible .aux.xml Persistent Auxiliary Metadata (PAM) file with band statistics. Recommended for ArcGIS Pro workflows.

param.name: add_to_map
param.dialogReference: Automatically add the optimized output GeoTIFF to the current ArcGIS Pro map after processing completes.

param.name: report_format
param.dialogReference: Output format for the comparison report. Choose HTML for a rich, interactive report with charts and formatting, or Markdown for a text-based report.

param.name: report_suffix
param.dialogReference: Suffix to append to the comparison report filename. Default is '_comp' (e.g., 'output_comp.html'). Use a custom suffix to organize multiple reports.

param.name: open_report
param.dialogReference: Automatically open the comparison report in your default browser (HTML) or text editor (Markdown) after generation.
